Hi All

Please see below and attached feedback on actions from yesterday’s meeting.

Regulatory Confirmation 

	*	The angle sensor requirement applies in Europe and Israel but is not mandatory for the UK, avoiding unnecessary procurement for UK vehicles.



I checked with Stuart and although the angle sensor is not a requirement for the UK market, we are going to have the angle sensors on F-Series as standard for the UK market. So we will have to work these into the recommended parts list for P700.

Digital Process Improvements 

	*	Proposal from ITUK to develop an online portal for tracking technical and parts queries submitted to IML, replacing the current email-based process. 
	*	The concept will be proposed to Japan and evaluated together with IT to improve transparency and response times.

 

ISZE presented the development of a portal system at the 2024 EU Aftersales conference (refer attached and screenshot below). Has there been any progress on this portal since it was presented in 2024? 



 



 

*	Engine & Cab Parts 

Please see attached “VIN List 23_07_2026”. Is it possible for our colleagues at IML to populate the complete engine, cab with electrics and cab without electrics part numbers and send back to us? This would reduce the amount of time required to quote for cabs and engines in the future.

 

James is going to send the forecast information for dealer sales tomorrow.

Hi Jerome

I've responded to each of your questions below on my view of the UK market across both vehicles and parts.

 

1. Customer sentiment vs. 6 months ago

 

Sentiment has noticeably softened. Six months ago we were seeing reasonably steady enquiry levels on the vehicle side and customers were broadly willing to commit to orders within their planning cycles. Today, conversations are taking longer, decisions are being deferred, and customers are asking more questions around total cost of ownership, residuals and lead times before they commit. The current geopolitical situation is part of it, but it's compounding pressures that were already there, interest rates, cost of living increases, and uncertainty around the broader UK economic and political outlook. Seems we again might have a Prime Minister change on the horizon if I listen to the news this weekend and that has historically not been good for customer confidence.

 

On the parts side, the picture is somewhat different. Operators are keeping vehicles in service longer, which is supporting aftersales demand, but customers are increasingly price-sensitive and we're seeing more scrutiny on parts pricing, more requests for quotes against alternatives, and pressure on the dealer network to remain competitive against independent factors \ aftermarket suppliers.

 

2. Impact of rising fuel prices on purchasing decisions

 

Yes, we are seeing a visible impact. For our customer base, predominantly SME operators and owner-drivers in the 3.5t–7.5t segment, fuel is a significant proportion of operating cost, and any sustained increase puts pressure on margins quickly. Some observations from our recent management meetings being,

 

*	Customers are extending the life of existing vehicles rather than replacing on their usual cycle.
*	More scrutiny on fuel economy when discussions are taking place around specification.
*	Some softening in finance approvals as operators' cashflow positions tighten.

From an ITUK perspective, the rationale for ISZE’s €10,000 contribution is not based on a direct or immediate financial return from the UK market alone, but rather on supporting a strategic initiative that strengthens genuine parts sales and retention for both ITUK and ultimately also ISZE.



The platform is designed to address future parts sales opportunities, for example targeting 3rd party repairers to claw back business currently going to factor parts suppliers like CV Components. A significant proportion of lost sales to the aftermarket is driven not by price, but by convenience and availability. By improving the ordering experience we expect to:

*	Increase order frequency from existing dealer and fleet customers
*	Improve retention of genuine parts by reducing leakage to factors
*	Provide a route to market for independent repairers who are currently outside of the network

 

In terms of financial return, while it is difficult to attribute a precise figure at this early stage, our expectation is that a relatively small uplift in parts sales will cover the €10,000 investment within a short period. This situation is extremely concerning from a customer and market perspective.

 

Delays of this magnitude simply do not occur with other manufacturers in the UK when ordering a replacement cab. If the lead time is likely to extend to eight months or more before the cab can even be supplied, most insurance companies will simply write the vehicle off rather than wait for the repair to be completed.

 

The longer-term risk for us is that once a vehicle is written off, the customer often replaces it with another brand. Situations like this therefore have a direct impact not only on parts sales but also on future vehicle sales and overall brand confidence in the market.
